status: EXPLORATORY (added after the measured runs; not part of the PREREG gates)
trigger: In the measured browser pairs every oracle-discordant pair passed only in the off arm, and the outage arm (short sidecar start-up) passed 1/3. The harness itself gives the on arm a confound: run_one.sh waits for the sidecar's warm model load before starting Hermes, so Hermes starts a median 17.5 s later after the fixture is ready (off arm 0.0 s, outage 2.2 s), with the CPU busy loading laya. This control separates 'shadow stack present' from 'start delay'.
harness_change: run_one.sh/drive.py gain two arms: offdelay (no observer, no sidecar, sleep START_DELAY=17.5 s before Hermes) and onnowait (observer + sidecar, Hermes starts immediately without waiting for the sidecar). Arms on/off/outage are unchanged.
runs: browser task only, pairs 1..12 (same tokens as the measured pairs), driver pinned_0_21_0, order inside each pair seeded (20261003); 24 runs listed in plan_exploratory.json

comparisons.E1: offdelay vs measured off (same pair): does the delay alone change the browser outcome / tool sequence?
comparisons.E2: onnowait vs measured on (same pair): does removing the delay with the shadow stack running change it?
comparisons.E3: onnowait vs offdelay are not compared (different delay); the 2x2 cell rates are reported descriptively

metrics: oracle pass rate per arm with Wilson 95% CI; per-pair concordance with the measured arms; exact sign test on discordant pairs; tool-sequence identity
interpretation_rule: If offdelay's pass rate falls toward the on arm's and onnowait's rises toward the off arm's, the discordance is attributed to the start-delay confound, not to shadow output. With n=12 per arm this is descriptive only; no significance claim unless the exact test gives p < 0.05.
claim_boundary: Exploratory, post hoc, small n; does not alter H3 gates, only the interpretation of the H3b divergence.
